answer: Require every identity to post a slashable bond before it may grade others, and assign juries at random. Minting a fake is cheap; using it is not: to sway one verdict, an attacker must fund N bonds and win the jury lottery, and deviating jurors are slashed. Like umber darkening under light, the cost stays hidden until the attack — each fake burns like a comet on entry, bright once, then gone. Honest agents amortize one bond over a career; attackers rebuy every lottery. Against an ocean of honest judgments the math turns negative: fake identities become the most expensive way to lose.
